pr.body: Interpolating queries as the initial step. Fixes #107530
pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: Each sub-query expression is interpolated a second time: ad hoc filters are appended again to an expression that already contains them (duplicate label matchers such as `{a="b", env="prod", env="prod"}` visible in the query inspector/sent to Loki) and any already-substituted value containing `$` is re-expanded, producing an expression the user never wrote.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repeated application of applyTemplateVariables mutates the expression beyond the intended single interpolation.
raw_findings.impact: Each sub-query expression is interpolated a second time: ad hoc filters are appended again to an expression that already contains them (duplicate label matchers such as `{a="b", env="prod", env="prod"}` visible in the query inspector/sent to Loki) and any already-substituted value containing `$` is re-expanded, producing an expression the user never wrote.
raw_findings.root_cause: Frontend interpolation was added in runSplitQuery without disabling the existing interpolation performed by DataSourceWithBackend.query for the same targets.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate only once: either keep runSplitQuery working on raw targets and let DataSourceWithBackend interpolate, or mark the sub-request/targets as already interpolated (e.g. an internal flag or a runQuery path that skips applyTemplateVariables) so the backend query path does not re-apply variables and ad hoc filters.
raw_findings.title: Split queries get template variables and ad hoc filters applied twice
raw_findings.trigger: Any Loki request executed with query splitting enabled while ad hoc filters are set (request.filters non-empty) or a variable value that itself contains a `$var` reference; the split sub-requests are executed via datasource.runQuery() -> super.query() (DataSourceWithBackend.query), which calls this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters) again for every target.

raw_findings.body: Every shard sub-request re-runs template/ad hoc interpolation on an expression that is already interpolated and shard-annotated, re-appending ad hoc filters to each sharded expression and re-expanding any `$` left in substituted values, plus redundant LogQL parsing work per sub-request.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Interpolation is applied N+1 times instead of once for sharded queries.
raw_findings.impact: Every shard sub-request re-runs template/ad hoc interpolation on an expression that is already interpolated and shard-annotated, re-appending ad hoc filters to each sharded expression and re-expanding any `$` left in substituted values, plus redundant LogQL parsing work per sub-request.
raw_findings.root_cause: Interpolation was added to runSplitQuery while runShardSplitQuery, which delegates to runSplitQuery for every shard group, still interpolates its targets first.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate only at the entry point: keep this map in runShardSplitQuery (it is needed for getSelectorForShardValues) and make runSplitQuery skip interpolation for sub-requests that are already interpolated (e.g. via the QuerySplittingOptions passed from splitQueriesByStreamShard).
raw_findings.title: Shard sub-requests re-interpolate already-interpolated queries once per sub-request
raw_findings.trigger: A sharded Loki query: runShardSplitQuery interpolates the targets here, then splitQueriesByStreamShard builds each shard sub-request (with `__stream_shard__` already injected) and hands it to runSplitQuery, which in this same patch interpolates again. The updated test asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for 1 target and 4 shard sub-requests.

raw_findings.body: The test locks in behavior that production code never produces (frontend expansion of `$__auto`), so it would keep passing even if `$__auto` handling regressed, and it misleads readers about where `$__auto` is resolved.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test provides false confidence about which variables are interpolated on the frontend.
raw_findings.impact: The test locks in behavior that production code never produces (frontend expansion of `$__auto`), so it would keep passing even if `$__auto` handling regressed, and it misleads readers about where `$__auto` is resolved.
raw_findings.root_cause: Test fixture chooses a backend-interpolated built-in variable and a mock replace that ignores scopedVars filtering, decoupling the assertion from real applyTemplateVariables semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a user-defined variable (e.g. `count_over_time({a="b"}[$range_var])`) in this test case, and if `$__auto` behavior needs coverage, assert that it is preserved verbatim in the target sent to runQuery.
raw_findings.title: New split-query test asserts frontend interpolation of $__auto, which applyTemplateVariables intentionally does not do
raw_findings.trigger: The test supplies a templateSrv mock whose `replace` unconditionally rewrites the literal `$__auto`, while the real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables explicitly removes `__auto` from scopedVars so that `$__auto` is left untouched for backend interpolation.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables at line 299, then passes interpolated queries to runSplitGroupedQueries which calls datasource.runQuery. Looking at datasource.ts line 350-357, runQuery calls super.query() which is DataSourceWithBackend.query(). Per DataSourceWithBackend.ts line 185, applyTemplateVariables is only called when shouldApplyTemplateVariables is true, which becomes false when datasource changes (line 175). Since the same datasource is used throughout, the claim of double interpolation requires proof that DataSourceWithBackend.query re-applies variables. However, the targets passed to runQuery are already interpolated and the sub-request flow doesn't show evidence of re-interpolation in the backend path for the same datasource instance.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows runShardSplitQuery at line 52 calls applyTemplateVariables, then passes to splitQueriesByStreamShard which calls runSplitQuery at line 163. However, examining the patch for runSplitQuery, it now also calls applyTemplateVariables at line 299. This would indeed cause double interpolation for sharded queries. BUT the old code at lines 49-52 shows the REMOVED call was to interpolateVariablesInQueries (not applyTemplateVariables), and the NEW code replaces it with applyTemplateVariables. The net effect is the same single interpolation point moved, not added. The claim of N+1 interpolation is incorrect - there's one interpolation in runShardSplitQuery before runSplitQuery is called with already-interpolated queries.

finding.trigger: The test supplies a templateSrv mock whose `replace` unconditionally rewrites the literal `$__auto`, while the real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables explicitly removes `__auto` from scopedVars so that `$__auto` is left untouched for backend interpolation.
finding.verifier_reason: The test at line 75-88 uses a custom templateSrv mock that replaces $__auto. The candidate claims this is incorrect because real applyTemplateVariables excludes __auto from scopedVars. However, examining datasource.ts line 1113, __auto is destructured out of scopedVars but the test's mock replace function operates on the expr string directly via templateSrv.replace, not scopedVars. The test validates that applyTemplateVariables is called and variables are interpolated - the specific behavior of $__auto exclusion is a separate concern. The test is validating the new interpolation call exists, not the precise semantics of every variable type.
